subject: MSA & Order Form — security exhibit redline handback and pen-test window plan
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthplus.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@healthplus.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Security exhibit redlines + SOC2 / pen test clarifications

Jordan —

Thanks for sending the draft security exhibit earlier. We reviewed and added a few redlines (attached redlines_from_HP.pdf) around the audit rights section and pen-test language. Two items we need clarified before our procurement team will sign: 

1) Penetration test windows — we want to lock a 7-day staging window with mutually agreed calendar dates and 72-hour notice for test start. Please confirm Redwood's ops support during the window and whether you require rolling access or ephemeral creds.

2) Evidence cadence — our auditors expect weekly evidence drops for the first 60 days after go-live (SOC 2 artifacts, key rotation logs, and pen-test remediation status). We need to confirm retention and delivery mechanism (SFTP vs secure share).

We attached our redlines and included Rahul from procurement for scheduling. Can you confirm what language you'll accept versus what needs legal review on your side?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Director, InfoSec — HealthPlus
ellen.park@healthplus.com
Attachment: redlines_from_HP.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthplus.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@healthplus.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines + SOC2 / pen test clarifications

Ellen —

Appreciate the quick review and the marked redlines. High level: we can accept a bounded pen-test window and an agreed 72-hour notice, but there are a couple of operational details to lock down (credentialing model and rollback plan). On evidence cadence, we can deliver weekly artifact bundles for the first 60 days into a secure S3 share with IAM-limited links, or we can push to an SFTP endpoint if you require pull access. 

Two asks from our side so legal can sign off more quickly: 
- Can HealthPlus accept a carveout that limits inspection to non-production tenants unless a critical incident is suspected? (helps with multi-tenant risk).
- For pen-test scope, can we agree to a pre-test attestation period where both parties confirm scheduled scope and excluded systems (e.g., third-party-managed infra)?

I cc'd Laura for legal language and Ben for ops details. Proposed next steps: Laura to propose redline language by EOD tomorrow, Ben to propose credential flow and draft runbook by Wednesday, and then loop back for a mutually available pen-test window (we're aiming for late Nov).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthplus.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@healthplus.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines + SOC2 / pen test clarifications

Ellen / team —

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed the file and drafted alternative language that preserves HealthPlus's need for assurance while keeping Redwood's multi-tenant and operational constraints in mind. Key changes attached (HealthPlus_SecExhibit_v2.docx). Summary of the proposed compromises: 

- Limited inspection: we propose "bounded inspection rights" that allow HealthPlus access to platform evidence and SOC 2 artifacts and the ability to request an on-site or remote inspection only where reasonably necessary and agreed in advance. We included a clause that requires Redwood to provide equivalent evidence for production systems where feasible, and if access to multi-tenant production is requested, we offer a scoped sampling and redaction process.

- Penetration testing: we accept a 7-day staging window and 72-hour notice for tests against Redwood-managed staging environments. For production-facing tests, we recommend a separate controlled engagement with a shared runbook and pre-test attestation 14 days prior. We added language that liability for disruptive testing is limited to direct damages attributable to Redwood's negligence.

- Evidence cadence & delivery: we agree to weekly evidence bundles for 60 days post-go-live. Delivery mechanism: secure S3 share with time-limited downloadable links to objects and audit logging. We included an alternative SFTP workflow in the exhibit if HealthPlus prefers pull access. Retention: SOC 2 artifacts retained for 12 months after request, KMS rotation logs retained for 6 months by default (can extend on request).

Laura attached tracked changes and a clean copy. Specific items we'd like HealthPlus to accept or drop to expedite sign-off: the unrestricted production inspection clause and the unlimited liability carveout in the pen-test section. If you accept the bounded inspection and limited liability as redlines, legal can sign the exhibit and we can schedule ops coordination.

Requested timeline: please confirm acceptance of the redlines by COB Friday 2025-10-17. If accepted, Ben will coordinate a tentative pen-test window (proposing Nov 23-29) and send a runbook.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: HealthPlus_SecExhibit_v2.docx
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@healthplus.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@healthplus.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines + SOC2 / pen test clarifications

Laura / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the tracked exhibit. We discussed internally and HealthPlus can accept the bounded inspection language with the sampling/redaction process. We also accept the staging-window approach and the pre-test attestation for production tests. One outstanding ask: can Redwood commit to a one-week SLA for providing mitigation evidence after a medium/high finding is reported? Our security team needs that for procurement.

If you confirm the one-week mitigation-evidence SLA and the Nov 23-29 tentative window works for ops, Rahul will circulate a clean order form for signature and we will move to DocuSign. Attached is a short procurement checklist for your reference.

We appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to finalizing.

Ellen Park
Director, InfoSec — HealthPlus
ellen.park@healthplus.com
